question: What is the primary clinical definition of urinary incontinence?

options.C: The complete inability to produce urine
options.D: An infection of the urinary bladder

explanation: Urinary incontinence is specifically defined as the involuntary leakage or loss of urine. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h1)

question: Why do many elderly patients in Nigeria often fail to report urinary incontinence early?

options.A: Hospitals do not treat urinary tract issues
options.B: The symptoms disappear without medical treatment
options.C: Diagnostic tests are too expensive to perform
options.D: They consider it a normal part of aging

explanation: Many individuals delay seeking help because they mistakenly believe leaking urine is an inevitable part of growing older. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h1)

question: Which part of the nervous system helps the bladder relax so it can store urine?
explanation: The sympathetic nervous system promotes detrusor muscle relaxation and sphincter contraction so the bladder can hold urine safely. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h2)

question: What happens in the bladder and urinary sphincter when a person urinates normally?

options.A: Both the detrusor and sphincter relax completely
options.D: Both the detrusor and sphincter contract together

explanation: Urine leaves the body when the bladder muscle contracts while the outlet sphincter relaxes to open the passage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h2)

question: A patient leaks urine when coughing or lifting heavy market loads. What type of incontinence is this?
explanation: Stress incontinence occurs when physical pressure from coughing or lifting overcomes weak pelvic floor muscles. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h3)

question: What is the underlying mechanism responsible for overflow urinary incontinence?

options.B: Physical inability to walk to the toilet
options.C: Weakened pelvic floor support from childbirth
options.D: An overdistended bladder that fails to empty

explanation: Overflow incontinence occurs when urinary retention fills the bladder past capacity, causing continuous minor leakage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h3)

question: Which condition is a major contributing factor to urinary incontinence in aging men?
explanation: Enlargement of the prostate gland obstructs the urinary outlet in men, frequently causing overflow or urge incontinence. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h4)

question: How can chronic constipation contribute to urinary incontinence?

options.A: Hardened stool blocks the flow of urine in the urethra
options.B: The straining weakens the abdominal wall muscles permanently
options.C: Constipation causes severe dehydration and concentrated urine
options.D: Stool pressure in the rectum irritates the adjacent bladder

explanation: An impacted bowel exerts physical pressure against the urinary bladder, triggering involuntary bladder contractions. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a voiding diary during clinical assessment?

options.A: To measure the exact weight of the patient daily
options.B: To record fluid intake, leakage frequency, and triggers
options.C: To track the patient's daily diet and nutritional status
options.D: To calculate the total kidney filtration rate over time

explanation: A voiding diary helps nurses and doctors identify patterns, fluid habits, and specific triggers associated with leakage episodes. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h5)

question: Why is a urinalysis routinely performed during the evaluation of urinary incontinence?

options.A: To measure the exact bladder muscle thickness
options.B: To rule out active urinary tract infections
options.C: To assess the strength of the pelvic floor
options.D: To determine the patient's neurological status

explanation: Urinary tract infections can cause acute irritation and symptoms that mimic or worsen incontinence, so infection must be excluded. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h5)

question: What is the main goal of teaching a patient Kegel exercises?
explanation: Kegel exercises specifically target and strengthen the pelvic floor muscles to improve urinary sphincter control. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h6)

question: How does a timed voiding schedule help a patient with urge incontinence?

options.A: It eliminates the need for pelvic floor muscle training
options.B: It prevents the bladder from filling past the trigger point
options.C: It stretches the urethra to make passing urine easier
options.D: It completely stops the kidneys from producing urine

explanation: Scheduled voiding empties the bladder at regular intervals before unmanaged urgency and involuntary leakage can occur. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h6)

question: Which class of medication is commonly prescribed to calm an overactive bladder muscle?
explanation: Anticholinergic drugs reduce bladder contractions and help manage symptoms of urge urinary incontinence. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h7)

question: Why is topical estrogen sometimes prescribed for postmenopausal women with incontinence?

options.A: To increase the total volume of urine produced daily
options.B: To improve the health of urethral and vaginal tissues
options.C: To prevent the development of kidney stones
options.D: To stimulate voluntary contractions of the abdominal wall

explanation: Estrogen deficiency causes thinning of urogenital tissues, and topical application helps restore structural support and tissue health. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h7)

question: What skin problem often happens when urine stays in contact with the skin for too long?
explanation: Constant exposure to urine irritates the skin, leading to rashes, sores, and moisture-associated skin breakdown. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h8)

question: What should be the nurse's main focus when dealing with the emotional impact of incontinence?

options.A: Reducing social stigma and supporting patient dignity
options.B: Focusing solely on surgical treatment options
options.C: Ensuring the patient stays indoors at all times
options.D: Reporting the condition to public health authorities

explanation: Because patients often experience shame and isolation, nursing care must prioritize emotional support and dignity. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h8)
